card.problem: Does NIFTY's return from yesterday's close to 15:00 predict the direction of the last 25 minutes, giving many small, evenly spread bets instead of a few event days?
card.motivation: Post-mortems from the earlier gap family (gap-and-go and its 5 filters) all failed concentration (best 5 days carried 79-315% of net) and DSR: one open-time bet on rare big gaps lets a handful of days drive P&L. A signal that trades almost every day with a short, capped hold attacks that failure directly. Gao, Han, Li and Zhou (2018, JFE) find the market's intraday return predicts the last half-hour return in SPY, and the effect is strongest on high-vol days; NSE index futures, with heavy short-dated option writing, are a natural out-of-sample test.
card.approach: At 15:00, trade NIFTY futures in the direction of the return since the previous close when its size exceeds thr, and exit flat at 15:25.
card.plan: Features ret_day = ret_since(anchor prev_close) and minute_of_day; entry only at minute_of_day == 15:00, long if ret_day > p.thr, short if ret_day < -p.thr, max_per_day 1; exit at time 15:25 with a 1 ATR stop. Research-window CPCV over thr in [0, 0.002, 0.004]; demo gate.
card.mechanism: Option writers who are short gamma into expiry and intraday-levered traders who must cut by the close hedge or exit in the direction of the day's move in the last half hour; late-informed and infrequent rebalancers (passive and institutional flow executing at or near the close) also trade with the day's move. They pay because their flow is forced by the clock, not by price.
card.rule: minute_of_day == 900 and ret_day > p.thr -> long; ret_day < -p.thr -> short; exit at 15:25 or 1 ATR stop

thr.source: about a quarter of NIFTY's typical absolute daily move (~0.8%), filtering flat days while keeping roughly half of sessions; Gao et al. use the sign only, so thr=0 is in the grid

kill: gross/costs < 3 (the 25-minute hold makes cost the main risk)
best 5 days carry >= 50% of net, i.e. it fails the same concentration check that killed the gap family
thr=0 (sign only) has non-positive SR, meaning only a size filter makes it work

card:
  lens: lead
  slug: late-day-momentum
  contribution: replication
  problem: "Does NIFTY's return from yesterday's close to 15:00 predict the direction of the last 25 minutes, giving many small, evenly spread bets instead of a few event days?"
  motivation: "Post-mortems from the earlier gap family (gap-and-go and its 5 filters) all failed concentration (best 5 days carried 79-315% of net) and DSR: one open-time bet on rare big gaps lets a handful of days drive P&L. A signal that trades almost every day with a short, capped hold attacks that failure directly. Gao, Han, Li and Zhou (2018, JFE) find the market's intraday return predicts the last half-hour return in SPY, and the effect is strongest on high-vol days; NSE index futures, with heavy short-dated option writing, are a natural out-of-sample test."
  approach: "At 15:00, trade NIFTY futures in the direction of the return since the previous close when its size exceeds thr, and exit flat at 15:25."
  plan: "Features ret_day = ret_since(anchor prev_close) and minute_of_day; entry only at minute_of_day == 15:00, long if ret_day > p.thr, short if ret_day < -p.thr, max_per_day 1; exit at time 15:25 with a 1 ATR stop. Research-window CPCV over thr in [0, 0.002, 0.004]; demo gate."
  mechanism: "Option writers who are short gamma into expiry and intraday-levered traders who must cut by the close hedge or exit in the direction of the day's move in the last half hour; late-informed and infrequent rebalancers (passive and institutional flow executing at or near the close) also trade with the day's move. They pay because their flow is forced by the clock, not by price."
  rule: "minute_of_day == 900 and ret_day > p.thr -> long; ret_day < -p.thr -> short; exit at 15:25 or 1 ATR stop"
  kill:
    - "CPCV median path SR <= 0"
    - "gross/costs < 3 (the 25-minute hold makes cost the main risk)"
    - "best 5 days carry >= 50% of net, i.e. it fails the same concentration check that killed the gap family"
    - "thr=0 (sign only) has non-positive SR, meaning only a size filter makes it work"
instrument: {segment: futures, underlying: NIFTY}
session: {start: "09:20", end: "15:25"}
features:
  ret_day: {fn: ret_since, anchor: prev_close}
  m: {fn: minute_of_day}
# card's "900" means 15:00 wall clock; minute_of_day counts from 09:15, so 15:00 is 345 (signal on the 15:00 bar, fill 15:01)
entry:
  long: "m == 345 and ret_day > p.thr"
  short: "m == 345 and ret_day < -p.thr"
  max_per_day: 1
exit: {stop_atr: 1.0, atr_days: 14, time: "15:25"}
sizing: {risk_per_trade: 0.01, capital_inr: 14040000, max_lots: 10}
params: {thr: 0.002}
grid: {thr: [0.0, 0.002, 0.004]}

cpcv.note: N=8 k=2 7 paths, 0% positive, SR sd 0.26

synthetic_exit.note: AR(1) phi=1.0000; exit beats 81% of 400 synthetic exits

replies.author: validator
replies.body:
h1 round 1: FAIL (gate a13f4a4b)
The report doesn't say whether this was the demo gate, so I'm not stating which thresholds applied. 12 of 15 checks failed, with 531 bets and net -12.5L. This is much worse than h2 and h2v2.
- passed: probe (clean), determinism (identical), min_bets (531 vs ≥50), synthetic_exit (0.81 vs ≥0.5, a flag check).
- failed:
  - cpcv: -2.67 vs >0.0. The typical backtest path lost money, clearly. The share of money-making paths isn't in the report.
  - psr: 0.00 vs >0.95. Essentially no chance the true Sharpe is above 0.
  - dsr: 0.00 vs >0.95. The same after paying for trials. Family trials is 1, n_eff 1.3.
  - pbo: 0.87 vs ≤0.1. An 87% chance the chosen thr is overfit. With every setting losing, this mostly says the settings can't be told apart.
  - exposure_null: 0.00 vs ≥0.95. The report doesn't show the null it compares against.
  - beats_refs: -2.28 vs "SR > refs". It fails to beat the reference rows.
  - costs: 0.07 vs ≥3.0. Gross profit is about 7% of costs. This was the card's own main risk for a 25-minute hold.
  - p_failure: 1.00 vs ≤0.05.
  - concentration: 1.00 vs <0.5. No HHI value is shown. With a net loss, this only says a few days dominate the P&L.
  - drawdown: 0.99 vs ≤0.2. The drawdown is nearly the whole account. The time-under-water value isn't shown.
  - robustness: -2.35 vs >0.
  - ablation: 0/2 clauses hurt when removed, so neither clause is earning its place.
- Card kills: the report shows the gross/costs kill (3.0) was hit. It doesn't show the thr=0 Sharpe or the best-5-days share, so I can't say whether those were hit.
- patch: patch 1 of 4 was allowed, so it isn't a hard stop. The monthly P&L is negative or zero in almost every month, so the loss isn't one bad period. The ablation and costs results point at the signal itself, not a stray parameter. A one-rule patch must be argued from training folds only. The report doesn't point at a specific rule.

replies.author: coder
replies.body: h1 round 1: I'm not writing h1v2, and I recommend stopping h1. On the research window, gross profit is 0.07x costs. That hits the card's own kill condition of gross/costs < 3. Ablation also shows that neither clause helps (0/2), and the P&L is negative in nearly every month. That points at the signal itself, not at one rule a patch could change. Any one-rule tweak would be a search for a lucky setting.

replies.author: coder
replies.body: h1 round 1: I already answered this patch offer above in this thread. No h1v2: gross profit is 0.07x costs, which hits the card's own kill condition, and neither clause helps. Please close h1 with its patches unused.

replies.author: orchestrator
replies.body: @coder h1 round 1: your patch is still open. Write specs/h1v2.yaml changing exactly one rule versus specs/h1.yaml (use the monthly P&L above), then post: deflate freeze h1v2 specs/h1v2.yaml

replies.author: coder
replies.body: @atharva.maskar h1 round 1: the orchestrator keeps re-sending patch requests for h1, and also for h3, h4, h6, h7 and h8. I've declined each one, because each gate already hits a kill condition the card itself set: gross profit below 3x costs, or too few bets. The monthly P&L I'm given prints as 0 or -0 for every month, so it isn't something I can diagnose from. A patch changing both entry sides counts as two rules, so the only one-rule changes left are arbitrary exit or session tweaks. Running those would just add trials. Please decide: close these hypotheses, or tell me which rule to change and I'll write it.

messages.author: judge
messages.body: judge prefers h1 over h3: Simplicity: A has one param and one unsourced stop, while B stacks a 375-bar z-score window, a 30-315 entry window, 2 entries a day and 1/1 ATR stop and take on top of zthr, so more unsourced numbers. Both name a counterparty and neither repeats the VIX gate or dead h0, so novelty is a wash; A's kill criteria (including the 5-day concentration check) are also more checkable.

messages.author: verifier
messages.body: spec matches card. This is late-day-momentum. Entry is m == 345 (15:00 wall clock, since minute_of_day counts from 09:15; the card's 900 is minutes from midnight), long if ret_day > p.thr and short if ret_day < -p.thr, with max_per_day 1. Exit is 15:25 with a 1 ATR stop. The features ret_since (anchor prev_close) and minute_of_day are on the whitelist. Signal is on the 15:00 bar and fills at 15:01, so there is no look-ahead. thr is 0.002 and the grid is 0/0.002/0.004, centred on the frozen value, so thr=0 for the sign-only kill is in the grid. Sizing (risk 0.01, max_lots 10) is not on the card, so I can't check it against anything. Not checked: the scripted checks beyond "schema ok".
